review_type: Independent read-only semantic/source audit; no local compilation or proof edits
publication_status: Working files; not bound to a published commit in this review
verdict: Semantically sound within documented component scope; no hidden main-conclusion or termination hypothesis found.
findings: ParallelGreedy: matching labels and earlier-walk exclusion are genuine Definition1.1 data. Equal-length increasing walks with2r≤s+1 are unique by comparing final edge labels; this covers fixed-length Lemma3.3 including odd-s extension. No path-uniqueness assumption supplied.
ParallelGreedy appended short_cycle_max_twice: split at a max-label edge, use complementary cycle walk of length≤s, rule out all other labels strictly smaller. This is actual Lemma3.2.
DispersionCount: enumerates actual finite fixed-length walks, filters increasing labels, derives at most1 per ordered endpoint pair and exact n^2 upper bound. Not an assumed path-count function.

Cuts: integer witness size≤total node budget gives attained demandVolume via Nat.findGreatest; sparseCut requires positive volume explicitly, avoiding totalized zero division. Source nonzero-cut issue handled by relevant h≥0,s≥1 regime; zero decomposition allowed explicitly.

FiniteTermination: every positive-volume sparse cut removes a currently h-near ordered pair and cannot add one. Strong induction on concrete finite near-pair cardinality constructs maximal finite sparse sequence, with length bounded by initial count. No compactness, minimum increment, infinite sum, or termination oracle. Result concerns unscaled totalCut.

Node budgets are permitted more generally than source A≤degree; stronger generality is harmless for these results. Near/Far use actual walks and match source metric semantics for intended finite nonnegative lengths; no machine algorithm claim.
No end-to-end decomposition size/arboricity/union-of-cuts theorem is certified by these components alone.

additional_source_correction.issue: Source Thm5.1 scales a maximal sequence sum by1+1/(s−1), then infers expansion by maximality. Extra length increases need not preserve absence of sparse cuts.
